Turning the Expert’s Diagnostic Method into a Platform Anyone Can Operate

Producing a net-zero transition consultation and diagnosis report for SMEs has traditionally relied heavily on manual work: counsellors travelled to sites to copy equipment nameplate data, consulted catalogue specifications item by item, converted GHG emissions by hand, and repeatedly transcribed the same data between spreadsheets and documents — time-consuming, error-prone, with calculation processes that were difficult to trace, and report quality that depended on each counsellor’s individual experience.

This platform is based on the 2025 SME Programme for Enhancing Green Competitiveness in Response to the Net-Zero Carbon Trend, organised by the Small and Medium Enterprise Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs and implemented by the Industrial Technology Research Institute, “Consultation and Diagnosis Files for 30 Companiesas the empirical basis, its report structure, calculation methods and improvement-recommendation logic have been transformed into a visual, operable digital diagnosis platform. This page is the experience website for that platform: its layout, input fields, formulas and database are identical to the actual platform, and figures may be entered directly for instant trial calculation.

Principle 1: The Report Structure Is the Operating Structure

The layout follows the five sections in order — Reporting Data, Carbon Emissions Summary, On-Site Diagnosis, Annex I and Report Overview — and the operating sequence is the report’s chapter sequence, so there is no need to learn the report structure separately.

Principle 2: Minimum Input, Maximum Derivation

All items requiring manual input appear in yellow bold input boxes; enter only on-site measured values and key parameters. All other values are retrieved, converted, or derived by the system, and calculation results appear in blue cells, clearly distinguished from manual input.

Principle 3: Every Figure Traceable

Every calculation result is accompanied by the complete formula and the step-by-step calculation with substituted figures; every adjustable parameter in the formulas is clearly marked, and any figure can be recalculated and verified from the original inputs.

Expert-led; AI is only an auxiliary tool. On-site diagnosis, causal judgement of energy-consumption problems, selection of improvement measures, data review and signed responsibility for the report all belong to the expert’s assessment experience and professional knowledge; AI undertakes only auxiliary execution such as data retrieval, unit conversion, formula trial calculation and document generation. The value of this platform is that it digitises, computerises and platformises the expert’s method — the diagnosis framework, packaged formulas and solution logic distilled from 30 companies’ empirical evidence — as an interdisciplinary application of “Sustainability + AI”, rather than replacing the expert with AI.

Overall Workflow: Understanding How the Platform Works at a Glance

Six steps run from case creation through to report output; Steps 4, 5, and 6 each include an “expert judgement” node (on-site diagnosis and causal-logic building, improvement-measure selection, and report review with named accountability), the three databases below form the AI-assisted layer, and data from newly produced reports feed back into the databases, forming a feedback loop.

Electrical Equipment Replacement Plan

Fuel Equipment Replacement Measures

When fuel equipment is replaced by electric equipment (such as electric vehicles or electric heat pumps), the “Added Annual Electricity Cost After Replacement” must first be deducted, and the payback period is calculated on net annual savings: Payback Period = Investment Cost ÷ (Annual Fuel Cost Savings − Added Annual Electricity Cost).

Formula and Factor Engine: How the Data Behind Each Input Box Were Built

The platform’s calculation core consolidates the methods drawn from 30 diagnostic files into a single set of formulas and factors, verified formula by formula (of 13 formulas, 9 matched the original files exactly and 4 were corrected during verification; the corrected versions are shown in the table below). Every factor states its source, so anyone can recalculate and verify using the same set of formulas.

ItemFormulaParameters and Sources
Fuel Emissions (Full Factors)Emissions = Activity Data × (CO₂ Factor + CH₄ Factor × 27.9 + N₂O Factor × 273) ÷ 1000Factors are taken from the Ministry of Environment GHG Emission Factor Management Table, Version 6.0.4; GWP values follow IPCC AR6 (CH₄ = 27.9, N₂O = 273). The CH₄ and N₂O factors for vehicle gasoline/diesel differ from those for stationary combustion and must be distinguished by use — simplified factors counting CO₂ only would underestimate vehicle gasoline by 4.16% and vehicle diesel by 1.58%.
Purchased Electricity (Scope 2)Emissions = Annual Electricity Use (kWh) × 0.474 ÷ 1000The electricity emission factor of 0.474 kgCO₂e/kWh is the 2024 announced value.
Septic Tank (CH₄)Emissions = Number of persons × 0.003825 t CH₄/person-year × 27.9 = Number of persons × 0.1067 t CO₂e0.003825 t CH₄/person-year is a built-in factor of the template; multiplying by a GWP of 27.9 must not be omitted (an early version of the framework omitted this multiplication and understated the result by a factor of 27.9; this has been corrected).
Refrigerant LeakageEmissions = Annual Refill Quantity (kg) × GWP ÷ 1000GWP values follow IPCC AR6: R-22 = 1,960, R410A = 2,256, R32 = 771, R134a = 1,530, R407C = 1,908, R600a ≈ 3 (AR5 values would underestimate by 6.5%–12.5%).
Annual Electricity Consumption of EquipmentAnnual Electricity Use (kWh) = Power (kW) × Quantity × Annual Operating Hours × Load FactorPower is based on the nameplate “Power Consumption / Rated Input”; where only HP is marked, convert by × 0.7457 (1 HP = 0.7457 kW). A blank load factor defaults to 0.7, the default where no operating-rate data are available; where a measured operating rate exists, the measured value takes precedence.
Cooling Demand ConversionRefrigeration tons = Floor area in ping × Cooling capacity per ping ÷ 3,024; 1 RT = 3,024 kcal/h = 3.517 kWCooling capacity per ping by use: residential 450–500, office 500–550, shops 550–650, restaurants 650–800 kcal/h/ping; increase the value where there is western sun exposure, a top floor, or substantial heat-generating equipment.
Annex I: Electricity ReplacementAnnual electricity savings = (Current power − Improved power) ÷ 1000 × Quantity × Annual operating hours × Load factor; Annual electricity cost savings = Annual electricity savings × Electricity price; GHG reduction = Annual electricity savings × 0.474 ÷ 1000Annual Operating Hours = Months per Year × Days per Month × Hours per Day. The formula must include both the load factor and the quantity — an early version omitted them and, at a load factor of 0.7, overestimated electricity savings by 42.9%; this has been corrected.
Annex I — Fuel ReplacementAnnual Fuel Savings = Current Usage − Improved Usage; GHG Reduction = Annual Fuel Savings × Complete Factor ÷ 1000; Net Annual Savings = Annual Fuel Cost Savings − Added Annual Electricity Cost After ReplacementThe fuel price is entered by the user (the year or actual listed price should be noted); when fuel is replaced by electricity, the additional electricity cost must first be deducted for the net annual savings to be correct.
Payback PeriodPayback Period (years) = Investment Cost ÷ Annual Cost Savings (for fuel measures, Net Annual Cost Savings)When annual savings ≤ 0, “Not recoverable” is displayed; no negative or infinite values are output.

Full Fuel Factors (kgCO₂e/unit, calculated live by the platform):. Factor sources: Ministry of Environment GHG Emission Factor Management Table, Version 6.0.4, IPCC AR6 GWP, and the 2024 electricity emission factor announced value.

Worked Examples (Cross-Verified)

The inputs in all three examples below are actual file records, quotation data or data tabulated in journal papers, and have been recalculated and verified against the Formula Verification Report and the Cross-Validation Report; Example 2 is the pre-filled D03 Automotive Parts Manufacturing example above, covering the four measures in Table 4 of the journal paper. Of the 30 reports, only two companies — Automotive Parts Manufacturing and Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Engineering — had all six totals fully reconcile; errors in the other companies’ reports mostly lay in the reports themselves (miscalculations or totals not stated). The platform’s handling principles are: payback periods are always recalculated as net investment ÷ annual savings, missing inputs are marked “No data yet”, totals are marked “Platform-Calculated Value”, and platform-calculated values are not presented as reconciling with the reports.

Example 1: MAXE Air Conditioner MAS-72MV5 (Nameplate Example from the Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Engineering Industry)

  1. Old annual electricity consumption: 2.64 kW × 2,000 hours × load factor 0.7 = 3,696 kWh(Nameplate power consumption 2,640 W, CSPF 3.87; annual hours = 8 hours × 250 days)
  2. New Annual Electricity Consumption: 1.6 kW × 2,000 × 0.7 = 2,240 kWh(New unit assumed to be the same class, CSPF 6.0)
  3. Annual Electricity Savings: 3,696 − 2,240 = 1,456 kWh
  4. Annual GHG Reduction: 1,456 × 0.474 ÷ 1000 = 0.690 t
  5. Annual Cost Savings: 1,456 × Electricity Price NT$4.5/kWh = NT$6,552
  6. Payback Period: Investment CostNo data yet, not calculated

Example 3: Air Compressor Replacement Plan (Corrected Values)

  1. Annual Electricity Savings:144,155 kWh(Actual file record, entered directly; replaced with a 復盛 variable-frequency screw-type unit)
  2. Annual GHG Reduction: 144,155 × 0.474 ÷ 1000 = 68.329 t

Division of Labour Between Experts and AI: People Lead, AI Assists

This platform presents a dual contribution: the expert personally conducts the energy-saving diagnosis and assessment, while also inventing and building this method into an operable platform — placing the assessment items on the platform so that carbon inventory and energy-saving counselling become simpler and easier to use. This is precisely the interdisciplinary application of “Sustainability + AI”; but the focus of the argument always remains on people:

◆ Expert-led (Irreplaceable)

  • On-Site Diagnosis: walk into the plant to read nameplates, operating status, and process characteristics, and decide what to measure and inventory.
  • Causal Logic: build the causal logic chain for an energy-consumption problem first — whether it is equipment ageing, poor control, or process demand — before discussing solutions.
  • Measure Selection: Make the final judgement between investment, payback period, construction feasibility and subsidy conditions.
  • Review and Accountability: Each report is reviewed and signed by the diagnoser, who is responsible for the figures.

◇ AI-assisted (Handling Complex Execution)

  • Data Retrieval: Draft company profiles and product/process descriptions; check equipment specifications against the 438-record database first, and search online only if not found there.
  • Unit Conversion: HP ⇄ kW, ping ⇄ refrigeration tons, W ⇄ kW, with a consistent basis throughout.
  • Formula Trial Calculation: The packaged formulas derive annual electricity savings, GHG reduction benefits and payback periods in real time, with every calculation step visible.
  • Document Generation: reports and platform inputs are consolidated from the same source, eliminating errors from manual transcription.

The convenience lies here: report production shifts from item-by-item manual calculation to calculation upon input, returning counsellors’ time to on-site diagnosis and measure selection; accuracy is verifiable, because formulas, factors, and calculations are visible throughout and reviewers can recalculate and check them; the professional threshold is lowered, because the visual interface and step-by-step calculations guide the full process; and knowledge accumulates, because the equipment database and the solutions and subsidies knowledge base grow with every case, turning individual case experience into reusable organisational assets.

Data basis: the consultation and diagnosis files of 30 companies under the 2025 SME Programme for Enhancing Green Competitiveness in Response to the Net-Zero Carbon Trend, hosted by the Small and Medium Enterprise Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs and executed by the Industrial Technology Research Institute (Contract No. A31142102); an equipment database of 438 entries across 84 brands, 369 of which include a source link. Factor sources: the Ministry of Environment GHG Emission Factor Management Table, Version 6.0.4, IPCC AR6, and the 2024 electricity emission factor announcement. The pre-filled example on this page is the complete D03 automotive parts manufacturing data from Tables 3 and 4 of the journal paper “Carbon Inventory-Driven Energy-Saving Counselling for SMEs Towards Net-Zero Sustainability: An Economic Benefit Assessment”, shown by industry only, with the contact field left blank; total annual savings and the weighted payback period are platform-calculated values consistent with Table 4; the air-compressor replacement measure uses the corrected payback period of 2.60 years (the original report’s 2.06 years was in error); Scope 3 is not included in the system inventory.
